questions.text:
The value of [latex]\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi }{4}}x\cos (x^{2})dx[/latex] correct to three decimal places
(assuming that [latex]\pi[/latex]  = 3.14 ) is
questions.solution:
Substitute [latex]u=x^2[/latex], [latex]du=2x\,dx[/latex]:
[latex]\int_0^{\pi/4}x\cos(x^2)dx=\frac12\sin(x^2)\Big|_0^{\pi/4}=\frac12\sin\left(\frac{\pi^2}{16}\right)=\frac12\sin(0.616)\approx\frac12(0.578)\approx0.289[/latex]

Answer: 0.289

questions.text: Consider a matrix [latex]A=uv^{T}\; where \; u=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 2 \end{bmatrix},v=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]  Note that [latex]v^{T}[/latex]  denotes the transpose of v. The largest eigenvalue of A is _____.
questions.solution:
[latex]A=uv^T[/latex] has rank 1. [latex]Au=u(v^Tu)[/latex], so u is an eigenvector with eigenvalue [latex]v^Tu=1+2=3[/latex]; the other eigenvalue is 0.

Answer: 3

questions.text: Let G be a finite group on 84 elements. The size of a largest possible proper subgroup of G is ________.
questions.solution:
By Lagrange's theorem the order of a subgroup divides 84. The largest proper divisor of 84 is 42 (index 2).

Answer: 42

questions.text: The postorder traversal of a binary tree is 8,9,6,7,4,5,2,3,1. The inorder traversal of the same tree is 8,6,9,4,7,2,5,1,3. The height of a tree is the length of the longest path from the root to any leaf. The height of the binary tree above is ______.
questions.solution:
Postorder ends with 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] root 1. Inorder splits into left {8, 6, 9, 4, 7, 2, 5} and right {3}.
- Left subtree: root 2 (last in its postorder), with left {8, 6, 9, 4, 7} and right {5}.
- {8, 6, 9, 4, 7}: root 4, left {8, 6, 9} (root 6 with children 8, 9), right {7}.

Longest path: 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 = 4 edges.

Answer: 4
